clue.text: Lock up after a protest

indicators.note: the reversed lock is placed after the letter given by the word a

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word for lock is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: A jailer locks someone up after they have made a protest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lock' reads as a verb beside 'up', but it is a noun, a curl of hair; 'up' is the reversal signal for this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To protest one's innocence is to declare it firmly, a sense of protest meaning affirm or maintain.

clue.text: Rather badly stained

indicators.note: badly signals that the letters of stained are put together wrongly, in a new order

explanation.surface: A garment that is somewhat badly stained, perhaps by wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Rather, as in 'I'll have tea rather than coffee', means in place of or as an alternative.

clue.text: Controversial engagement event one might expect in Birmingham shopping centre?

definitions.text: Controversial engagement event one might expect in Birmingham shopping centre?

parts.words: Controversial engagement event one might expect in Birmingham shopping centre
parts.note: Birmingham's best-known shopping centre is the Bull Ring; a bullring is the arena where a contested animal fight is staged in Spain

explanation.surface: A puzzled shopper wonders what spectacle to expect at a big Birmingham mall.
explanation.walkthrough: The Bull Ring is a major shopping centre in Birmingham, England; read literally, a bull ring is where a Spanish bull and matador meet.
explanation.definitionFit: A matador's contest with a bull is a disputed spectacle, an engagement between man and animal staged in an arena.

clue.text: Throw buns — eating the majority

indicators.note: the answer takes up most of the letters of the two words buns and eating, so it sits inside them

explanation.surface: A child hurls buns at people while having eaten most of them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the majority' says the answer is most of 'buns eating': only the B and the final ING are left out.
explanation.definitionFit: To throw a rider is to dislodge them from the saddle, the same as removing them from their seat.

clue.text: For instance, going about a quiet walk in a showy way

indicators.note: the phrase for instance surrounds the other pieces, going round them

parts.note: say, as in 'a fruit, say an apple', means for instance
sh is the call for quiet

explanation.surface: Someone takes a quiet stroll, but does it ostentatiously.
explanation.definitionFit: To strut or flounce along with exaggerated hip movement is a swaggering, conspicuous way of walking.

clue.text: Some say 'Scrap Christmas programming'

indicators.note: some say signals that what is spoken is heard as a different written word

parts.note: to shed is to scrap or discard, and Yule is Christmas; spoken together they make the entry

explanation.surface: A headline: some people want to cancel Christmas television broadcasts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some say' marks a sound-alike: 'shed Yule' (scrap Christmas) is pronounced like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A broadcaster's programming is its timetable of shows, the planned list of what airs when.

clue.text: Males tormented witches once here

indicators.note: tormented signals that the letters of males are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: Men tormented women accused of witchcraft in a town long ago.
explanation.definitionFit: The Massachusetts town held notorious witch trials in 1692, so it is where witches were once said to be.

clue.text: On the same wavelength — and about to be accepted by getting on

indicators.note: one piece is taken in by the other, held within it

parts.note: getting on means growing old
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Two people are in tune, ready to be welcomed by others as they get along.
explanation.definitionFit: People on the same wavelength share views, so they concur with one another.

clue.text: Rosy is sober having downed half of stout

indicators.note: the word for sober swallows the other piece, which goes down inside it

parts.note: sane means sober or rational

indicators.note: half of means the first four of the eight letters of the stout's name

parts.note: Guinness is the famous Irish stout

explanation.surface: A rosy-cheeked drinker insists they are sober despite downing half a pint of stout.
explanation.walkthrough: Stout is a dark beer, and Guinness the best-known brand; the wordplay needs a synonym of the stout, not the word itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosy, as in a rosy outlook, means optimistic or hopeful, a sense shared with the answer.

clue.text: Chorale needs arrangement that's extremely infectious

indicators.note: needs arrangement says the letters of chorale are to be put in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A choral piece needs an arrangement that will make it catchy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'infectious' looks like praise for a catchy tune; here it is the disease.
explanation.definitionFit: This bacterial disease of the gut spreads rapidly through contaminated water, making it a highly contagious illness.

clue.text: Celebrate making it out of Essex to Lancashire

indicators.note: the answer is made out of letters found running through the words that follow

explanation.surface: Someone celebrates escaping Essex for Lancashire, two English counties.
explanation.walkthrough: Essex and Lancashire are English counties at opposite ends of the country.
explanation.definitionFit: To praise someone highly or sing their virtues is to celebrate them.

clue.text: Ideas came free in places of learning

indicators.note: free signals that the letters of ideas came are released into a new order

explanation.surface: Ideas flowed freely in universities and schools.
explanation.definitionFit: Schools, colleges and institutes of study are places where learning takes place.

clue.text: Demure lure of French is absent

indicators.note: is absent says the French word for of is taken away from the lure

parts.note: a decoy is a lure for game birds
de is French for of

explanation.surface: A shy, modest bait used in France is missing.
explanation.definitionFit: Demure and the answer both describe someone shy, modest and reserved, perhaps affectedly so.

clue.text: Spanish red wine poured over bit of cereal — attack with vigour

indicators.note: the wine is poured over and around the cereal piece, enclosing it

parts.note: tinto is Spanish for red wine, as in vino tinto
an ear is the grain-bearing head of a cereal plant

explanation.surface: A breakfast scene: red wine sloshed over cereal before someone tucks in.
explanation.definitionFit: To attack something with vigour, physically or in criticism, is an idiom for laying into it.

clue.text: Wail for guys being muscle-bound

indicators.note: the muscle is bound around the other piece, holding it inside

parts.note: lat is short for latissimus dorsi, a back muscle
guys are men

explanation.surface: Someone cries out on behalf of men who are muscle-bound.
explanation.definitionFit: A wail is a cry of grief, the same as an expression of mourning or sorrow.

clue.text: Reckoning guards caught habit

indicators.note: guards means one piece surrounds and protects the other

parts.note: addition is reckoning, adding up figures
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A day of reckoning as guards catch someone with a bad habit.
explanation.definitionFit: A habit in the sense of a drug habit is a compulsive dependence.

clue.text: Too young to be pinching booty, ignoring personal boundaries

indicators.note: ignoring says the letters that follow are left out

parts.note: plunderage is the stealing of goods, especially embezzlement aboard ship

indicators.note: the boundaries of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A youngster caught stealing loot, with no respect for others' personal space.
explanation.walkthrough: 'personal boundaries' gives P and L, the outside letters of personal, which are removed from the front of PLUNDERAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Too young for something, such as drinking or voting, means below the legal minimum age.

clue.text: Old man is missing by centre

indicators.note: is missing says the word by is absent from the other piece

parts.note: old man is slang for husband, informally hubby

explanation.surface: An elderly man has gone missing near the town centre.
explanation.definitionFit: A hub is the focal point or centre of activity, like the middle of a wheel.

clue.text: Mercenary Conservative avoids American questioning

parts.note: US stands for American, as in US troops

indicators.note: avoids means the abbreviation for Conservative is left out of the other word

parts.note: curious means inquisitive, questioning

explanation.surface: A grasping Tory politician dodges questions from an American.
explanation.definitionFit: Charging exorbitant interest on loans is a grasping, money-driven practice, so mercenary fits.

clue.text: Dismiss the odds of friend becoming communist

indicators.note: discarding the first, third and fifth letters of friend leaves the even-placed ones

explanation.surface: Ditch a friend's unlikely chances once they turn communist.
explanation.definitionFit: Red is the colour associated with communism, so it is a common informal label for a communist.

clue.text: Beginnings of Rolling Stones

indicators.note: rolling suggests the letters of stones tumble over into a new order

explanation.surface: The early days of the band the Rolling Stones.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as the famous rock band; 'Rolling' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Beginnings and starts of something, such as the first stages of an illness, are its commencements.

clue.text: Eat interminably, making loud noise

indicators.note: interminably means without its end, so the final letter of the word for eat is dropped

parts.note: to dine is to eat

explanation.surface: A noisy diner eats endlessly.
explanation.definitionFit: A din is a loud, prolonged, unpleasant racket.

clue.text: With slight disorder, been getting healthy — that's a perk

indicators.note: slight disorder says the letters of been are mildly jumbled

parts.note: fit means healthy

explanation.surface: Someone with a minor ailment has been recovering; there's an upside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With slight disorder' turns BEEN into BENE, a small swap of two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A perk is an extra advantage, such as a company car, a fringe reward on top of salary.

clue.text: I am explosive, with discontented night approaching

parts.note: I'm is the contraction of I am
a mine is an explosive device

indicators.note: discontented means the contents are removed, leaving only the outer letters of night

explanation.surface: A bomb boasts of being explosive as a restless night draws near.
explanation.definitionFit: Something about to happen very soon is near at hand, approaching.

clue.text: Daily Echo

definitions.meaning: the Daily ... is a British national tabloid newspaper
to echo is to copy or reflect back exactly

explanation.surface: Two newspaper titles side by side, the Daily and the Echo.
explanation.walkthrough: Both words look like newspaper names; Daily is the British tabloid's first word, Echo is a verb meaning reflect.
explanation.definitionFit: A British daily tabloid is named after the looking-glass, which reflects or echoes back an image.

clue.text: Hat — no tat!

parts.note: Cockney rhyming slang gives tit for tat for hat, shortened by dropping the final rhyming word

explanation.walkthrough: Cockney rhyming slang, from London, rhymes 'tit for tat' with hat and then drops the rhyme, 'tat', hence 'no tat'.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a British informal slang word for headgear, deriving from rhyming slang.

clue.text: Prince briefly holding back-to-back recordings — on one there's hot stuff

indicators.note: the prince's abbreviation holds the recordings inside it

parts.note: Pr is the short form of Prince
an EP is an extended-play record

indicators.note: back to back means the second recording faces the other way, read in reverse

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A prince holds two records back to back, and on one is a hot track.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back-to-back' sets two extended-play records against each other, the second turned round, so the pair reads as a palindrome inside the prince.
explanation.definitionFit: A spicy, peppery sausage often used as a pizza topping counts as hot stuff.

clue.text: Ashes could be reinvigorated with this game

definitions.text: Ashes could be reinvigorated with this
definitions.meaning: a fire iron stirs dying embers back to life
a card game played for stakes

explanation.surface: England could revive their Ashes cricket campaign with this game plan.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ashes is the England-Australia cricket series; here the ashes are those of a fire.
explanation.definitionFit: The fire iron and the bluffing card game share a name: one stirs embers, the other is played with chips.

clue.text: Message, small, delivered in double time

indicators.note: the small piece is delivered inside the two time letters
double means the letter for time appears twice

parts.note: wee is Scots for small

explanation.surface: A short message delivered at twice the normal speed.
explanation.definitionFit: A short post on a social media platform is a brief online message.

clue.text: Third-rank rugby players bet on racket

parts.note: to back a horse is to bet on it
a row is a racket, a noisy disturbance

explanation.surface: Rugby forwards place bets on a tennis racket.
explanation.walkthrough: In rugby union the forwards line up in three ranks; the third is made of the flankers and number eight.
explanation.definitionFit: The flankers and number eight form the third and last line of a rugby scrum.

clue.text: Farah to increase power

parts.note: Mo Farah is the British Olympic distance runner
taken as written
a rise is an increase

explanation.surface: Mo Farah, the British Olympic runner, aims to boost his power.
explanation.definitionFit: To power a vehicle with an engine is to equip it with a motor.

clue.text: Nice pad — downsized chez Lynam?

definitions.meaning: estate agents' shortening of desirable residence, a nice home
the home of broadcaster Des Lynam, his residence, cut short

explanation.surface: A smart flat, now smaller: has the TV presenter moved house?
explanation.walkthrough: Des Lynam is a British TV sports presenter; chez means at the home of.
explanation.definitionFit: Estate agents' clipped jargon for an attractive house to live in, an appealing home for sale.
